title: Tenant-aware fuse to limit retry amplification during regional GPU thermal events
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In past regional degradation drills we observed retry amplification from client SDKs and our control plane resulting in cascading load that starves remaining GPU pools during a partial region outage or thermal-induced GPU throttling. This ticket implements a tenant-aware fuse (per-tenant adaptive circuit breaker + shedding) to reduce cross-tenant amplification while preserving SLOs for high-priority customers.

Goals:
- Prevent a noisy tenant or client SDK retry storm from exhausting healthy GPU pools during region loss or GPU pool exhaustion.
- Keep p95 latency and tail error budget within SLO targets for high-tier tenants.
- Provide observability to trace fuse activations and automated rollback paths.

Scope: design+implement fuse runtime + chaos test harness that simulates: region cutover, GPU thermal spike (reduced throughput), and a dependency blackhole (simulated control-plane slowdowns).
hypothesis: If we enforce per-tenant adaptive fuses that consider recent token consumption, retry signals, and priority tier, then during region-level GPU scarcity the system will avoid cascading failures and maintain SLOs for prioritized tenants, reducing global error budget burn by >40% compared to current baseline.
acceptance_criteria: During chaos runs (region cut + 30% GPU capacity drop + dependency blackhole) high-priority tenants retain >= 95% of their baseline successful qps and p95 latency increase < 2x baseline.
Overall cross-tenant error budget burn decreases by >= 40% vs baseline run with no tenant fuse.
Fuse activations are visible in Console heatmap, with tenant-level tracing and an alert firing within our SRE channel when >5% of active tenants have open fuses.
Automated rollback (open->closed) works and does not introduce stuck-open states after region recovery.
PRD, playbook, and runbooks linked and reviewed by SRE and PM.
experiment_plan:
1) Implement lightweight per-tenant token-bucket based fuse in edge admission controller with thresholds: in-flight token limit, recent retry-rate window, and priority weight.
2) Instrument metrics: tenant_inflight, tenant_retry_rate, fuse_state, fuse_open_count, shed_rate_by_tenant.
3) Run local regression to validate correctness.
4) Chaos harness: a) simulate region loss by gating one region's ingress and progressively move traffic, b) introduce synthetic GPU thermal event lowering available concurrency on a GPU pool, c) create dependency blackhole by delaying control-plane calls to 5s for 20% of requests.
5) Run three phases: baseline (no fuse), experimental (fuse enabled, conservative thresholds), tuned (adjust thresholds per run).
6) Collect metrics and dashboards for p50/p95/p99 latencies, success_rate, queue_depth, GPU_util, and overall token spend.
7) Execute canary rollout: 5% tenants -> 25% -> 100% with manual gate checks.
runbook:
- Pre-checks: ensure test cluster has observability retention for 48h and canary tenants created.
- Ramp plan: enable in staging, run chaos script for 10 minutes, validate metrics, then proceed to canary.
- If p95 exceeds threshold by >3x or user-visible errors spike for high-tier tenants, immediately disable tenant fuse and abort test.
- Post-mortem: collect traces, heap profiles, admission controller logs and open follow-up ticket if stuck-open observed.
mitigation_playbook:
Immediate: set fuse thresholds to permissive (increase token limits) or disable per-tenant fuse via feature flag.
Short-term: divert low-priority tenants to degraded model variants and enable queue shedding.
Long-term: expand inference admission controller to include cross-tenant fairness and a staged retry-backoff signal to SDKs.
comments: 2025-01-24 - Maya Li: SRE review - flagged that the fuse must persist minimal state across restarts (use Redis slot). Recommend adding jitter to reopen timers to avoid sync waves.
2025-01-28 - Ruben Ortega: Implemented initial token-bucket admission. Local tests show correct shedding behavior under synthetic surge. Pushed experimental PR for review.
2025-02-03 - Priya Shah (PM): Confirmed acceptance criteria alignment with customer SLAs; requested runbook addition for opt-in by enterprise customers to prefer throughput vs latency.
2025-02-10 - Security review: No customer data in fuse state; KMS not required. Marking security_review_required=false in metadata.
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive shedding protects healthy pools but may surface client errors for low-tier tenants. We prioritize preserving high-tier SLOs; future work will explore graceful client-visible degraded responses (structured error + retry-after headers).
next_steps: Finalize PR, schedule staging chaos run week of 2025-02-17, gather metrics, and iterate thresholds. Coordinate with SDK team to add explicit Retry-After semantics for fuse-triggered rejects.
